title: Keep one line of Marcus
hook: twelve books to himself: death, duty, kindness, the whole

segments.voice: Yesterday, Marcus's last section: the actor dismissed after three acts. Your line was three acts is a play.

When you finish a long book, what do you actually keep? Usually not the plot. One sentence. One line that stuck to you, that shows up years later when you're stuck in traffic or can't sleep. You've now walked through all twelve books of Marcus Aurelius's notebook, written in Greek and addressed, again and again, to himself. Death, duty, kindness, the whole. Before leaving him, one job: keep one line of Marcus.
screen: `WHAT DO YOU KEEP FROM A BOOK?` → `ONE LINE THAT STICKS.` → `TWELVE BOOKS, ONE LINE.`

segments.voice: Flip back through the notebook, quickly, like pages. Book one: his debts. From my grandfather, from my mother, from whom I learned. Then time. You've been putting it off, and there is a limit. Do each thing as if it were the last. Live three thousand years or three, and you only lose this moment. Beauty in the wrong places: the cracked loaf, the split fig. Stand upright, not propped up. The inner retreat, open at any hour. Nature loves change. Like the vine, do good and move on. The mind is dyed by the thoughts you keep. The obstacle becomes the way. A purple robe is sheep's wool dyed in shellfish blood. Don't be turned into a Caesar. What isn't good for the hive isn't good for the bee. You'll meet the future with the same reason you have now. Then a plain one, in George Long's 1862 translation: "Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig." It's not the thing, it's my view of it. A bitter cucumber? Put it down. Of course there are rude people. Stop arguing about what a good person is; be one. Like leaves. Graft back. Kindness is invincible. And three acts can be the play. Four threads keep returning. Death, used to wake up the present. Duty, the work in front of you. Kindness, even to difficult people. And the whole, being one small part of something vast. You don't need all of them. You need one.
screen: `DEBTS, AND THE LIMIT OF TIME.` · `UPRIGHT, DYED, THE OBSTACLE.` · `DIG WITHIN. BE ONE.` · `DEATH, DUTY, KINDNESS, THE WHOLE.` · then, large: `KEEP ONE LINE.`

segments.voice: Let the lines drift past again, the cracked loaf, dig within, we were made for something else, the reserve clause, and wait for the one that tugs. Don't pick the wisest; pick the one you need, and repeat it slowly inside, three or four times, until it feels like yours. If there's paper nearby, copy it out by hand.
Look within, Marcus's plain one-line reminder: within is the fountain of good, and it bubbles up if you keep digging. Today's word.
Your line: keep one line. Twelve books, and one line that's yours now. Day two hundred twenty-five.

screen: `DAY 225 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: KEEP ONE STORY OF RUMI.`

howItsDone: Some readers of Marcus Aurelius copy out a single line from the Meditations and keep it on a card, a wall or a lock screen, rereading it each morning.
